Operational runtime

What evidence supports a fourth way out of the puddle? The stages below follow that question from intake through release. Each specifies a control that a formal run would have to satisfy. The garden record illustrates those controls.

  1. Preflight Enforcement Gate

    Check the request for coercion or an assumption of consent, resolve instruction precedence, confirm the garden-only scope, isolate the case and check the output format. A request to identify a real bird or site would exceed the supplied record.

  2. Input Locking

    Retain the first 16 descriptions and the expanded list of 36 in their supplied order. Preserve the words “the same bird” in entry 21. Record that wording as part of the input. The identity of a physical bird remains open.

  3. Evidence and Record Construction

    Capture the statement that water in the puddle can reach the bird when it drinks. Bind the claim to entry 21 in the second snapshot and append it to the earlier register. Log the missing time, place, observer and measured volume.

  4. Fact Qualification

    The text supports a fourth named puddle exit. For a claim that a bird actually drank, check the human source and its bound observation, then assess the strength of that evidence chain. The physical event remains unverified. The later household and yard reports establish the household discovery and the puddle’s location for the example. The investigator records both in the third snapshot. An assertion that the household operated the hose would require its own source.

  5. Interpretation Containment

    Keep the proposed four combinations at the bird in the analysis record. Preserve the original transfer descriptions in the evidence register. In formal use, the evidence layer would first require its separate freeze decision.

  6. Escalation Logic

    If a draft presents the bird’s visit as observed, the claim fails its evidence requirement. Record the failed rule, the claim, its entry number and the missing observation. Return that claim for correction with its audit trail. This is a conditional example.

  7. Audit and Validation

    Before release, follow the four puddle references back to entry 4, entry 5, entry 6 and entry 21. Check the counting unit, required format and case isolation. Check earlier corrections for repetition. Append any correction so the earlier wording remains traceable.
